title: Enhanced cleaning under added controls for infection spread
audience: Cleaning staff who work in isolation rooms, cohorted areas and any area where a patient has an infection that requires added precautions.
learningOutcomes: List the additional controls layered over baseline practice when an infection spreads by touch, droplet or air.
Set out the cleaning expected in an acute area when an infection is suspected or confirmed.
State how long transmission-based precautions stay in effect.

instruction.heading: What the added controls involve
instruction.body: These controls apply to patients who may carry, or do carry, an infection passed by touch, droplets or airborne particles. They are always layered over baseline controls. When one illness travels by several routes, several sets are combined.

instruction.heading: The measures in acute settings
instruction.body: On an acute ward, the bundle of transmission-based measures comprises: baseline controls maintained; protective items chosen to fit the route (gloves, gown or apron, surgical or P2 masks, eye protection); equipment reserved for one patient; a private room or grouping with others infected by the same agent; air-handling as specified; intensified scrubbing and disinfecting the patient's immediate area; and limits on transfers within and between sites. Route-specific protection is detailed within B2.2 through B2.4, which should be read before use.

instruction.heading: Environmental cleaning under precautions
instruction.body: On an acute ward where a possible or verified agent needs transmission-based precautions, scrub surfaces with detergent mix, then apply a TGA-listed product suited to hospital use, using the two-step or two-in-one technique. In clinics and calmer settings, facility policy weighs contamination odds, transmission route and danger to people nearby before choosing disinfection.

instruction.heading: Duration
instruction.body: Transmission-based precautions last for a set span: until the symptoms have eased, or as infection control specialists advise for that organism. Never end a precaution on your own view; that call belongs to the infection prevention or clinical team.

instruction.heading: Crockery and utensils
instruction.body: Dishes and cutlery from a patient managed under these added controls need no special holding. They are handled like anyone else's and go through the dishwasher. Disposable tableware is unnecessary.

procedure: Check the patient's precaution sign and the facility's instruction for the room before you go in.
Put on the protective equipment the precaution requires, in the correct sequence, before entering.
Clean the room: a physical detergent clean first, then the approved disinfectant step, by the two-step or two-in-one method.
Pay close attention to frequently handled spots in the room, including handles, switches, the bed and the locker.
Remove protective equipment at the doorway or in the anteroom, following “PPE for cleaning tasks: choosing, putting on and taking off”.
Log the room, the precaution sign and the cleaning performed, and never remove the precaution sign yourself.

workedExamples.situation: You are asked to clean a room where a patient is on contact precautions for a multi-resistant organism. The door has a precaution sign and a wall-mounted gel dispenser.
workedExamples.reasoning: Check the sign and the facility instruction. Put on gown and gloves in the correct order, then clean the handled surfaces with a detergent step followed by the approved disinfectant. On leaving, remove gloves first and clean your hands, then the gown, then clean your hands again. Do not remove the sign yourself.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves, gown or apron, and mask or eye protection as the precaution sign specifies
TGA-listed disinfectant suited to hospital use, with the label claim for the organism
Clean cloths and single-use wipes as the facility directs

commonErrors.error: Beginning the clean with disinfectant by itself.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean physically with detergent first, then apply the disinfectant.

commonErrors.error: Treating a precaution sign as optional.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the sign and the instruction every time you enter.

commonErrors.error: Ending a precaution because the room looks clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Precautions end when the clinical team or infection prevention team says so, not when the room looks clean.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Transmission-based precautions sit on top of baseline controls and never take their place. Do not walk into a marked room unless you carry the gear the sign specifies.
Use only a TGA-listed disinfectant suited to hospital use, with a label claim for the organism concerned. Follow the label's wet contact time.
The clinical team decides on limits to patient movement. Do not take a patient or kit out of a precaution room without instruction.

qualityStandard: Learner checks the precaution sign and the instruction before entering.
Learner cleans with a detergent step followed by the approved disinfectant.
Learner removes protective equipment in order, with hand cleaning at each stage.
documentationEvidence: Enhanced clean record with room, precaution type and products used
Record of any missing protective equipment and the referral
summary: The added controls are layered on baseline practice according to how the infection travels.
On an acute ward with a confirmed or possible infection, scrub with detergent first, then apply an approved disinfectant.
Precautions end on clinical advice, not on the look of the room.

knowledgeChecks.question: How do transmission-based precautions relate to baseline controls?
options: Transmission precautions take over from routine checks
The added controls sit on top of baseline controls.
Baseline controls apply only without added controls.
They are unrelated, and each replaces the other on the ward.

knowledgeChecks.question: In an acute area where an infection requiring added precautions is known, how is the environment cleaned?
options: With a disinfectant alone, sprayed on the surfaces and left to dry on each surface, with no cleaning first at all
With a physical detergent clean, then a TGA-listed disinfectant suited to hospital use, by a two-step or two-in-one method.
With alcohol, applied to each surface once in the morning, with no detergent used at any stage of the work
With water and a damp cloth, then left to dry naturally, and no disinfectant is used at all in the room

knowledgeChecks.question: Who decides when the added controls can stop?
options: The cleaner, once the room looks clean and the patient has said they feel fine and the visitors have left
The clinical team or infection prevention team, based on the settling of signs and symptoms or the agent's advice.
The patient, on request, once they feel better and after they have eaten a meal and had a walk
The visitor who asks about the room and any staff member who passes the door at the time of the clean
